title: Hardware handoff: afternoon jitter and prep
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the afternoon handoff — mix of things I want to remember, quick commands, small experiments to try tonight, and questions for on-call. Not formal runbook, just raw reminders.

High-level status (right now):
- 6 GPU nodes in pool-a (p4d-like) are healthy, 2 nodes in pool-b reporting intermittent NVLink flaps (node-34, node-37).
- Autoscaler: healthy, target 18 -> 18. Observed two short spikes at 13:22 and 14:05 that queued for ~260ms then drained.
- Network: MTU mismatch flagged on edge-router-2; suspected VXLAN fragmenting for some pods.

Immediate TODO (prioritize):
1) Tag node-34/37 for investigation and put on maintenance schedule if NVLink repeats. Quick triage: collect dmesg + nvidia-smi topo --matrix, attach to ticket. (est 20–30m)
2) Run mtu check on edge-router-2 and adjacent veths: show ip link, test path MTU to 10.12.4.0/23. Add note to keep-safe: avoid rebless during working hours. (est 10m)
3) Confirm autoscaler policy didn't overshoot on short spikes — reconcile metrics with prometheus: query: max_over_time(pod_request_cpu[5m]). If pattern repeats, tighten scaleDownDelay. (est 25m)
4) Night experiment: try reduced kernel preemption on two canary GPUs to see if NVLink stability improves (kernel params snapshot, run for 2 hours). Mark as "canary-quant". (est 3h, low priority)

Quick commands to paste in Slack / ticket:
- Collect node info:
  sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "1h" --no-pager > /tmp/node-34-nvidia.log
  nvidia-smi -q > /tmp/node-34-smi.txt
  nvidia-smi topo --matrix > /tmp/node-34-topo.txt
- MTU checks:
  ip link show dev eth0
  sudo ip route get 10.12.4.8
  tracepath -n 10.12.4.8 | head -n 10
- Autoscaler metrics (promql):
  sum by(cluster) (rate(kube_pod_container_resource_requests_cpu_cores[2m]))
  increase(kube_pod_container_status_ready[5m])

Notes / observations (raw):
- Node-37 shows transient ECC errors in dmesg around 13:20 but disappeared after a restart. Could be thermal spike or BIOS microcode. Keep an eye — not yet reproducible.
- Pod churn pattern: lots of short-lived jobs from team "research-bench" — maybe the batch runner's backoff is too aggressive and triggers autoscaler thrash. Chat with Alex tomorrow.
- I bumped the CUDA driver on pool-b two nights ago; confirm driver/firmware combinations match pool-a. Mismatch can cause NVLink oddities.

Handoff messages to leave for night on-call:
- If NVLink errors reappear on node-34/37: cordon node, run full diagnostics (nvidia-smi -q, dmesg, sensors), open JIRA-OPS-2147, attach logs, mention thermal/firmware checks.
- If autoscaler spikes > 500ms request queueing: temporarily increase cluster maxBurst by 1 and file a follow-up PR to revert later.
- If MTU fragmentation persists: revert VXLAN to underlay MTU 1500 for the two affected hosts; notify network team.

Open questions / reminders to follow up:
- Ask SRE: do we have a per-node throttling config for nvlink-heavy workloads? (Slack @oncall-sre)
- Check with firmware team if a microcode drop happened last week (git tag /release notes).
- Try a short run with L2 cache disabled for the canary jobs to isolate ECC vs NVLink.

Personal notes (brain dump):
- Keep the handoff short and actionable. Highlight one critical ask for night: "cordon node-34/37 if NVLink returns".
- Capture commands and where logs live so any new night engineer can act quickly.
- If I get time tonight, sketch a mini playbook for "NVLink transient errors" that lists quick triage steps + escalation map.

Appendix (short cheats):
- kubectl to cordon: kubectl cordon node-34 && kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force node-34
- quick GPU health: watch -n 2 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,index,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv,noheader
- collect system snapshot: tar czf /tmp/node-34-snapshot.tgz /var/log/nvidia* /var/log/syslog /etc/modprobe.d /proc/driver/nvidia

End of scratchpad. Will clean up into proper runbook if this repeats.
